blocks.note: Choose an infinitive or a finite que clause by identifying whether the governing and subordinate predicates share a subject.
Recall which governed infinitives take no preposition and which select a, de, en, por, or another fixed link.
Interpret preposition-plus-infinitive phrases and switch to a finite clause when the subordinate action has a distinct subject.
Use a masculine singular infinitive phrase as a clause argument rather than copying an English gerund mechanically.
Contrast an infinitive that is itself the subject with adjective-plus-de constructions whose expressed subject is interpreted as the infinitive's object.
Choose verbal and adjectival participle forms while applying agreement only outside compound haber tenses.
Interpret compact participle clauses and keep lexical -nte adjectives distinct from productive gerunds.
Form regular and spelling-changing gerunds, then classify their adverbial link as time, manner, condition, cause, purpose, or concession.
Choose infinitive, gerund, relative clause, or another idiomatic form for perception and English -ing contexts.
Read the aspect contributed by andar, ir, llevar, quedarse, seguir, venir, and acabar before a gerund.
Translate English -ing modifiers with an established -nte adjective, a relative clause, a noun, or another lexical expression rather than an automatic gerund.
